blocks.heading: A booklet is a list
blocks.body:
Last week you wrote three pages. A **map** is a table of contents that **points at** those pages. The file ends in `.ditamap`.

It is not a copy of the words. It is a list of pointers.

The sample shop already has `samples/flower-docs/flowers.ditamap`. Open it. Look. Count. Do not add anything yet.

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
You just met the idea. Now do the lab: Look at the sample booklet.

This lab can fail. Fail when: You only opened a topic file and never opened the .ditamap, or you cannot say the booklet is a list of pointers.

Expected: You opened flowers.ditamap, counted the pages it points at, and opened one page from the tree.

blocks.lead: Walk the cards below, in order, to Look at the sample booklet.
blocks.intro: How to Look at the sample booklet. Walk the cards in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Look at the sample booklet
steps.body: This is the whole move. The next cards are the steps, in order.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: In Oxygen, open samples/flower-docs/flowers.ditamap. If it opens as a wall of tags, look for a booklet view (DITA Maps Manager) and open it there too.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Count how many pages the booklet points at. Write the number in oxygen-bootcamp-work/week3/day-15-count.txt.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Click one line in the tree so the page opens. Confirm it is one of the topic files, not the booklet file itself.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Do not add a page yet. Today you only look.

options: A table of contents that points at page files
The same thing as a how-to page
blocks.why: The map is the booklet. The topics are the pages. Two kinds of files.

blocks.lead: Answer with words from today only.
blocks.q: If you delete a page file but leave it in the booklet, what happens?
options: Nothing :  the booklet has a copy of the words
The pointer breaks. The booklet still names a file that is gone
Oxygen reprints the page from memory
blocks.why: The booklet stores a pointer (a path), not a second copy of the page.
